title: Odyssey, TI-99/4A and FM Towns discovery
summary: Review an old Llamasoft discovery task and three rotated repository-search routes; add ten source-backed projects across Odyssey/Videopac, TI-99/4A, C64 and FM Towns.
notes: The CPU audit queue returned zero unresolved source or target CPU areas before candidate selection. Exact successful fresh-search queries were `Odyssey2 assembly`, `Videopac source code`, `TI-99 assembly` and `FM Towns homebrew`; narrower disassembly/reconstruction variants returned no repositories. Candidate promotion counts reflect ten repositories whose primary README/source was actually reviewed, not raw search hits. The current mwenge/Llamasoft graph was rechecked against the catalogue; its known repositories remain covered, while the broader C64-Mark/non-C64 neighbor task stays open.

sources.reason: Fresh-search slice. Exact queries `videopac disassembly OR odyssey2 disassembly`, `videopac disassembly`, and `odyssey2 disassembly` returned no repositories; broader exact queries `Odyssey2 assembly` and `Videopac source code` surfaced four new URLs. Primary README/source review promoted giogu75/asm_8048, korb3n70/odyssey2026, lab1702/odyssey9 and gameblabla/videopac-soren-stuff.

Fresh-search slice rotated from the earlier TI-99 disassembly query to original assembly/homebrew and development tooling. The exact query `TI-99 assembly` returned nine new URLs; primary README/source review promoted visrealm/vrEmuTms9918, Nouspikel/Assm9TN9, Nouspikel/Lib9TN9, kenfitz/ti99-dev-suite and kenfitz/ti-snake-asm-cart. Remaining hits were screened but not counted as reviewed candidates.

Fresh-search slice. Exact query `FM Towns homebrew` surfaced gameblabla/FMTOWNSCD_EXAMPLE; its README, Makefile and implementation were reviewed and promoted. The narrower queries `FM Towns homebrew tooling` and `FM Towns source code` produced no additional repository candidates.
VS Code language support for Intel 8048 assembly used by Odyssey2/Videopac development.
Original C64 6502 tribute that reconstructs six Odyssey 2100-style games from scratch.
ROM-free behavioral reimplementation of Odyssey² Computer Intro!/Videopac 9 from the cartridge manual and examples.
Preserved Søren Gust Videopac/Odyssey/G7400 source, assemblers and documentation, including buildable 8048 source for Kill the Attacking Aliens.
C99 TMS9918/TMS9928/TMS9929 video-display-processor emulator core with CMake build and tests.
Object-oriented TI-99/4A TMS9900 cross-assembler with source, executable distribution and programming extensions.
TI-99/4A object-module librarian for the Link9TN9 cross-linker.
VS Code TI-99/4A development environment with TMS9900 language services, xdt99 builds, packaging and emulator launch.
Source-published TI-99/4A assembly fan conversion of the Apple II game SnakeByte with documented cartridge build.
Buildable i386 C/assembly FM Towns Marty CD homebrew example with ISO layout and emulator run path.

source_updates.reason: Llamasoft and adjacent reconstruction profile; its current known title repositories remain covered after a focused profile/index search.
C64 disassembly trail; the existing Hunchback record remains the verified canonical C64-Mark project while broader neighboring work still needs a direct profile inventory.

task_updates.notes_append: Focused searches rechecked the mwenge/Llamasoft title graph: the currently surfaced Gridrunner, Matrix, Iridis Alpha, Psychedelia, Ancipital, Return of the Mutant Camels, Voidrunner and Uridium repositories all resolve to existing catalogue records. C64-Mark/non-C64 neighboring titles still lack a complete profile inventory, so the task remains open rather than being closed on incomplete connector enumeration.

project.title: ASM 8048
project.display_title: ASM 8048 — VS Code language support for Odyssey² / Videopac
project.status: Published VS Code syntax-language support for Intel 8048 Odyssey2/Videopac assembly

identity.narrative: The repository README identifies asm_8048 as a Visual Studio Code extension providing ASM8048 language support for Odyssey2/Videopac development.

classification.narrative: This is original retro-development language tooling, not a disassembly or reverse-engineered subject.

source_cpu.narrative: The extension authoring project does not analyze an original executable with a source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly names Intel 8048 assembly as the language supported for Odyssey2/Videopac code.

build.narrative: The checked package and README establish a VS Code extension with syntax support; no assembler, compiler or generated ROM is claimed.
build.limitations: The extension was not installed during this pass.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed README and package metadata state no minimum host CPU or memory requirement.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and package metadata contain no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: No predecessor, successor or bundled assembler relationship is established by the reviewed project documentation.

project.title: Odyssey 2026
project.status: Source-published C64 tribute with six playable game modules and an ACME build path

identity.narrative: The README presents Odyssey 2026 as a Commodore 64 revival of the 1978 Magnavox/Philips Odyssey 2100 with six game modules.

classification.narrative: The author explicitly calls it a from-scratch reconstruction and tribute rather than a port; it is recorded as original fan homebrew, not as reverse-engineered or RE-derived.

source_cpu.narrative: The reviewed primary documentation identifies the Odyssey 2100 inspiration but does not state an original CPU architecture; none is inferred from the console name.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly says the implementation is pure 6502 assembly for the Commodore 64.

build.narrative: The README supplies an ACME command that builds odyssey2026.prg and documents the six selectable games and controls.
build.limitations: The tracker did not assemble or execute the program.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README documents Commodore paddle controls but no minimum CPU generation, RAM amount or chipset revision beyond the C64 target.

ai.narrative: The inspected README contains no development-AI disclosure; absence is not treated as evidence of non-use.

relationships.narrative: The README states the project is inspired by the Odyssey 2100 games but reconstructed from scratch for C64 rather than derived from their source or binaries.

project.title: Odyssey² Computer Intro! emulator

runtime_profiles.name: Desktop build
runtime_profiles.notes: The README requires Go 1.27 or newer; macOS additionally needs Xcode command-line tools, while Linux needs X11, OpenGL and ALSA development headers for building. No host CPU or RAM minimum is stated.

project.status: ROM-free manual-based reimplementation with assembler, disassembler, monitor, tests and four built-in games

identity.narrative: The README identifies a Go emulator of Magnavox Odyssey² Computer Intro!, also sold as Philips Videopac 9 Computer Programmer.

classification.narrative: The project implements the teaching computer from its manual without ROM files, including its instruction set, operating modes, examples and built-in games; it is a manual-derived behavioral reimplementation rather than a console ROM disassembly.

source_cpu.narrative: The implementation reconstructs the cartridge's documented teaching virtual machine rather than executing or translating an original hardware CPU binary.

target_cpu.narrative: The Go desktop implementation is cross-platform and the reviewed documentation does not define a fixed output CPU architecture.

build.narrative: The README requires Go 1.27+, supplies build/test commands for Windows, macOS and Linux, and documents ROM-free execution, monitor features and four built-in games.
build.limitations: The tracker did not build or execute the emulator.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The README states the build environments and host-side dependencies for Windows, macOS and Linux but no minimum host CPU or RAM.

ai.narrative: The inspected README contains no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The README ties the project to Computer Intro!/Videopac 9 and explicitly says the behavior is built from the cartridge manual, which is not included.

project.title: Søren Gust Videopac/Odyssey source archive
project.display_title: Søren Gust Videopac / Odyssey development archive
project.status: Preserved multi-component Videopac/Odyssey development archive with a documented ASL/p2bin ROM build

identity.narrative: The repository README attributes the archived Videopac/Odyssey/G7400 material to Søren Gust; the inspected KTAA source identifies Kill the Attacking Aliens for G7000/G7400 and carries Gust's copyright.

classification.narrative: This is a historical original-source and development-material archive, not a binary-derived reconstruction by the repository mirror author.

source_cpu.narrative: The preserved KTAA source explicitly selects `cpu 8048`, establishing the native historical architecture for that reviewed component.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed 8048 assembly is rebuilt by the KTAA Makefile into bank objects and a concatenated ROM for G7000/G7400 hardware.

build.narrative: The KTAA Makefile documents ASL assembly of four .a48 banks, p2bin conversion and concatenation into ktaa.rom.
build.limitations: Only the KTAA build component was examined in depth; the archive was not built or executed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The inspected archive documentation and KTAA source establish G7000/G7400 targets but no minimum RAM, firmware revision or other runnable hardware floor.

ai.narrative: The reviewed source is dated 2003 and presented as preserved historical work by Søren Gust; development-AI assessment is not meaningful for that historical artifact.

relationships.narrative: The mirror explicitly preserves Gust's material and notes one missing G4700+ slideshow archive; KTAA is one reviewed title component within the broader collection.

project.title: vrEmuTms9918
project.status: Zero-dependency C99 VDP emulator library with CMake builds and tests

identity.narrative: The README identifies vrEmuTms9918 as a zero-dependency C99 emulator core for TMS9918, TMS9918A and TMS9929A video display processors.

classification.narrative: This is reusable component-emulation tooling directly useful to retro emulator and hardware development, not a complete TI-99/4A emulator or a game project.

source_cpu.narrative: The emulated subject is a video display processor, not a CPU architecture.

target_cpu.narrative: The portable C99 library has no fixed generated output CPU; the reviewed documentation describes API integration rather than a target instruction set.

build.narrative: The README documents CMake configure/build and ctest commands and enumerates implemented video modes, sprites, collisions, VSYNC and scanline rendering.
build.limitations: The tracker did not compile or test the library.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum host CPU, RAM or operating-system requirement is stated for the C99 library.

ai.narrative: The inspected README contains no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The README identifies use by the PICO9918 replacement hardware and the HBC-56 emulator, while keeping this repository scoped to the shared VDP core.

project.title: Assm9TN9
project.status: Source-published Windows cross-assembler with executable distribution, macros, procedures and object-oriented extensions

identity.narrative: The README identifies Assm9TN9 as an object-oriented cross-assembler for creating TI-99/4A assembly on a PC.

classification.narrative: This is original retro-development toolchain software, not a reconstructed historical assembler or reverse-engineered subject.

source_cpu.narrative: The cross-assembler does not analyze an original executable with a source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The implementation explicitly defines a CTMS9900 assembler object and the legal 9900 opcode table, establishing TMS9900 output independently of the broad TI-99/4A platform label.

build.narrative: The README documents the distributed assm9tn9.exe interface and supporting initialization/macro files; C++ source and a Visual Studio 4.2 make project are present.
build.limitations: The historical compiler setup was not reproduced and compilability from source remains unverified.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed material identifies a PC executable but no minimum Windows version, host CPU or RAM.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and implementation header contain no development-AI disclosure; absence is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The README points to companion initialization, object-oriented and structured-error-handling source files and to the author's TI technical pages; no predecessor assembler derivation is claimed.

project.title: Lib9TN9
project.status: Source-published librarian for Link9TN9 libraries with interactive, scripted and command-line operation

identity.narrative: The README identifies Lib9TN9 as a librarian utility for Link9TN9 and TI-99/4A assembly programs.

classification.narrative: This is original retro-development toolchain software that creates and edits reusable object-module libraries.

source_cpu.narrative: The librarian is development tooling and does not analyze an original binary with a source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The reviewed README identifies TI-99/4A object modules and Link9TN9 but does not explicitly state the encoded CPU architecture; no TMS9900 value is inferred from platform alone.

build.narrative: The README documents a downloadable executable and interactive, script and command-line modes; C++ sources and a legacy make project are present.
build.limitations: The historical build environment was not reproduced, so source compilability remains unknown.

runtime_profiles.narrative: No minimum host operating system, CPU or memory requirement is stated for lib9tn9.exe.

ai.narrative: The inspected README contains no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The README explicitly places Lib9TN9 beside the Link9TN9 cross-linker and attributes its library model to the original RAG linker concept by R. A. Green.

project.title: TI-99/4A Development Suite
project.display_title: TI-99/4A Development Suite — VS Code build and emulator environment

runtime_profiles.name: VS Code extension host
runtime_profiles.os: Desktop Visual Studio Code with Python 3.8+ and xdt99 3.6.0+
runtime_profiles.notes: An emulator is optional for building but required for Build and Run. Primary documentation states no host CPU or RAM minimum.

project.status: Early but usable extension with language services, multi-route packaging and one-key emulator launch

identity.narrative: The primary README identifies a VS Code extension for writing TMS9900 assembly for TI-99/4A, building multiple artifact formats and launching emulators.

classification.narrative: This is original modern retro-development infrastructure, not a reverse-engineered game or historical-source reconstruction.

source_cpu.narrative: The environment creates new programs and packages source; it does not analyze an original executable with a source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The README explicitly states that users write TMS9900 assembly and documents the TMS9900 instruction set services.

build.narrative: The README documents source installation, xdt99-based builds, cartridge, E/A, TIFILES and disk-image outputs, artifact verification and emulator launch.
build.limitations: The extension and its external toolchain were not installed or executed in this pass.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Primary requirements are Desktop VS Code, Python 3.8+, xdt99 3.6.0+, and an optional emulator for run commands; no host CPU or RAM floor is given.

ai.narrative: The inspected README contains no development-AI disclosure; general language about an assistant-friendly template is not treated as evidence of AI use.

relationships.narrative: The README explicitly describes xdt99 as a separate required tool, identifies supported emulator integrations and credits the xdt99 IntelliJ plugin as a tokenizer reference.

project.title: TI Snake
project.display_title: TI Snake — TI-99/4A SnakeByte fan conversion
project.status: Source-published TI-99/4A assembly clone with documented cartridge image build

identity.narrative: The README identifies TI Snake as the author's TI-99/4A assembly clone of the Apple II game SnakeByte.

classification.narrative: The project is a source-published native fan conversion/reimplementation; the documentation does not claim disassembly, decompilation or other reverse-engineering derivation.

source_cpu.narrative: The README names the Apple II game inspiration but does not state the original game's CPU; no architecture is inferred from the Apple II platform.

target_cpu.narrative: The cartridge source explicitly labels its body `9900 CODE` and uses the TMS9900 register/opcode model, establishing the native target architecture.

build.narrative: The cart README documents producing a cartridge BIN with Asm994a and loading it in Classic99, including the exact assembler output options.
build.limitations: The tracker did not assemble or play the game.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed documentation names Classic99 as a run environment but gives no minimum physical TI configuration, host CPU or RAM.

ai.narrative: The inspected README and source contain no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The author describes the project as a clone of SnakeByte and the cartridge documentation identifies Asm994a and Classic99 as the build/run tools.

project.title: FM TOWNS MARTY CD example
project.display_title: FM TOWNS MARTY CD homebrew example
subjects: FM TOWNS MARTY CD homebrew example
project.status: Buildable FM Towns Marty CD image example with 32-bit protected-mode graphics and an emulator run script

identity.narrative: The README identifies an example FM Towns Marty CD program that loads an image from CD, draws it with double buffering and waits for vertical sync.

classification.narrative: This is original native homebrew and development-example code, not a reverse-engineered or RE-derived port.

source_cpu.narrative: The example is newly authored target software and has no analyzed original executable with a source CPU.

target_cpu.narrative: The Makefile explicitly invokes i386-pc-run386 GCC and assembler with `-march=i386`; the implementation describes 32-bit protected-mode execution.

build.narrative: The README and Makefile document the elf2exp toolchain, ISO build/run script and Tsugaru emulator path, with the explicit dependency on a user-supplied CD/IO.SYS.
build.limitations: The tracker did not supply IO.SYS, build the ISO or run the example.

runtime_profiles.narrative: The reviewed documentation identifies FM Towns/Marty and Tsugaru but gives no minimum physical CPU model, RAM amount, ROM version or host floor; the source's optional 486 cache path is not treated as a minimum.

ai.narrative: The inspected README, Makefile and implementation comments contain no development-AI disclosure; this is not a non-use claim.

relationships.narrative: The README requires pinterior/elf2exp for the toolchain and a user-provided FM Towns IO.SYS, and the run script targets Tsugaru; those dependencies are not bundled successors or forks.
